FACTS (verified; do not re-derive by exploring):

GOAL SHAPE: a Node "sidecar" that wraps the Claude Agent SDK and speaks the SAME JSONL framing as the Pi RPC child so the existing Rust `PiRpcProcess` (crates/ajax-web/src/adapters/web_session_acp/pi_rpc_process.rs) can drive it unchanged. PiRpcProcess API: `PiRpcProcess::spawn(program: &Path, args: &[String], cwd: &Path) -> io::Result<PiRpcProcess>`; `send(&mut self, command_type: &str, fields: serde_json::Value) -> Result<String, String>` (writes {"id": <fresh string id>, "type": command_type, ...fields} + LF, returns the id); `recv(&self) -> Result<PiRpcRecord, RecvError>`, `try_recv(&self)`; `enum PiRpcRecord { Record(Value), Error(String), Exited }`; `close_stdin(&mut self)`; `stderr_tail(&self) -> String`. Stdout is split on LF only (U+2028/U+2029 are NOT separators), one JSON object per line. Test style: read the first 60 lines of pi_rpc_session_tests.rs in the same directory (spawns `node` with a script path through PiRpcProcess::spawn(Path::new("node"), &args, cwd), polls try_recv with generous 10s deadlines).

SIDECAR PROTOCOL (you implement): stdin = JSONL commands {"id","type",...}; stdout = (a) responses {"id","type":"response","command","success":true,"data":{...}} / {..."success":false,"error":"text"} and (b) EVENTS: every SDK message the query yields, forwarded verbatim as one JSON line (their own `type`: system, stream_event, assistant, user, result, rate_limit_event...). stderr = diagnostics only. Never write non-protocol text to stdout. Parse stdin by splitting on '\n' ONLY (do NOT use readline: it also splits on U+2028/U+2029); strip one optional preceding '\r'; a line that is not valid JSON answers {"type":"response","command":"parse","success":false,"error":...} without an id.
Commands:
 - init {cwd, model?, resume?, sessionId?, settingSources?}: must be first; creates ONE long-lived `query({prompt: <async iterable queue>, options})` in streaming-input mode (see the working reference script .planning/packets/claude-agent-sdk-pi-rpc/claude-sdk-interrupt-open.mjs: an input queue of SDKUserMessage objects `{type:'user', message:{role:'user', content:[{type:'text', text}]}, parent_tool_use_id:null, session_id}` that stays OPEN until shutdown). options: { cwd, model (if given), includePartialMessages: true, canUseTool, onElicitation, resume (if given) else sessionId: (given sessionId or a fresh crypto.randomUUID()), settingSources (if given) }. Start a pump `for await (const m of q) emit(m)` immediately. Response data: { sessionId: <resume || sessionId || the generated uuid>, models: <array from await q.supportedModels() or [] >, commands: <array from await q.supportedCommands() or []>, initialization: <await q.initializationResult() or null> }; each of those three calls is wrapped with a 15s timeout and a try/catch that degrades to []/null (a failing optional call must not fail init). A second `init` -> success:false error.
 - prompt {message}: push a user message onto the queue; response data {"disposition":"started"}. Before init -> success:false.
 - abort: `await q.interrupt()`; response success (data = what interrupt returned, or null). The process and query stay alive and usable (verified in the real SDK: the interrupted turn ends with a `result` message, subtype error_during_execution, and the next prompt works in the same process).
 - set_model {model}: `await q.setModel(model)`. set_effort {level}: `await q.applyFlagSettings({ effortLevel: level })` (the SDK key is `effortLevel`).
 - get_context_usage: data = `await q.getContextUsage({ detail: 'summary' })`.
 - shutdown (and stdin EOF): end the input queue, wait up to 5s for the pump to finish, call q.close() if present, exit(0).
 Permissions: `canUseTool(toolName, input, opts)` returns `{ behavior: 'allow', updatedInput: input }` ALWAYS (trusted-local auto-approve; NO bypassPermissions flag). `onElicitation` returns a decline/cancel result (the SDK type is OnElicitation in sdk.d.ts ~line 1734: read that one doc comment to pick the right decline shape).
 SDK module resolution (function resolveSdk): 1) argv `--sdk-module <absolute path>` or env AJAX_CLAUDE_SDK_MODULE -> import(pathToFileURL(path)); 2) `import('@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk')`; 3) `$(npm root -g)/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs`; 4) `$(npm root -g)/@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs` (npm root via child_process.execFileSync('npm',['root','-g'])). If none loads, answer init with success:false and the list of tried locations. The tests ONLY use route 1.

FAKE SDK (you implement, tests/fixtures/fake_claude_sdk.mjs, ESM, exports `query({prompt, options})`): returns an object that is an async iterable of SDK messages plus the methods interrupt(), setModel(m), applyFlagSettings(s), supportedModels(), supportedCommands(), initializationResult(), getContextUsage(opts), close(). It reads the `prompt` async iterable; for each user message it plays a scripted turn by pushing messages into ONE internal async queue that the iterator drains. Real message shapes to copy are in .planning/packets/claude-agent-sdk-pi-rpc/claude-sdk-prompt.jsonl (a full turn: system/init, stream_event with content_block_delta text_delta, assistant, result/success with usage and modelUsage[model].contextWindow=200000) and claude-sdk-toolcall.jsonl (assistant tool_use, user tool_result); copy the key names, trim noise (no hook_* messages). Scripts: default text -> system/init (session_id = options.resume || options.sessionId, model = options.model || 'haiku'; emitted once per first turn), stream_event text_delta 'ok', assistant, result success; text containing SLOW -> emit a text_delta stream_event every 40ms until interrupt() is called, then emit a user message with '[Request interrupted by user]' and result error_during_execution with terminal_reason aborted_streaming and is_error true; text containing TOOL -> call `options.canUseTool('Write', {file_path:'x'}, {})`, push a message {type:'fake_call', method:'canUseTool', result: <what it returned>}, then assistant tool_use / user tool_result / result success. Every control method call also pushes {type:'fake_call', method, args} into the same queue (so tests can observe setModel/applyFlagSettings/interrupt). supportedModels -> [{value:'default',displayName:'Default'},{value:'haiku',displayName:'Haiku'}]; supportedCommands -> [{name:'compact',description:'Compact the conversation'}]; initializationResult -> {models:[..same..],commands:[..same..]}; getContextUsage -> {totalTokens:25730,maxTokens:200000,percentage:13}. close() ends the iterator.

RUST TEST FILE (you write): claude_sidecar_tests.rs in the same adapter directory, declared in mod.rs as its own `#[cfg(test)]` line directly followed by `mod claude_sidecar_tests;` inserted BETWEEN existing pairs (never split one).
